subject.title: [SECURITY] Privilege Escalation Vulnerability: docker Group Assignment Bypasses Hardening Measures

question: Which supported Docker trust model should OpenClaw Ansible guarantee: remove direct service-account access to a rootful daemon, retain it as an explicitly trusted boundary, or offer separately documented deployment modes?
rationale: The code change determines a core host-privilege boundary and can alter supported installation and operational workflows; source review alone cannot safely choose that security/usability contract.

options.title: Remove direct rootful daemon access
options.body: Move to a validated rootless-Docker or narrowly privileged deployment path so compromising the OpenClaw account does not directly grant host-root-equivalent Docker control.

options.title: Retain an explicit trusted boundary
options.body: Keep rootful Docker access only if maintainers intentionally treat the service account as host-administrative and revise the hardening claims and operational documentation accordingly.

options.title: Support documented deployment modes
options.body: Offer distinct trusted-rootful and hardened-rootless modes only if their upgrade, permissions, and operational differences can be kept clear and tested.

recommendation.title: Remove direct rootful daemon access
recommendation.body: Move to a validated rootless-Docker or narrowly privileged deployment path so compromising the OpenClaw account does not directly grant host-root-equivalent Docker control.

likelyOwner.reason: No feature-history owner could be established from the supplied review context; a repository security/deployment decision owner is needed.
